title: Mercurys Boot & the Stargate Tunnel
description: An off-track loop along the Capertee cliffline in Gardens of Stone National Park, taking in Mercurys Boot, Baal Bone Gap, McLeans Pass and the Stargate Tunnel.
lede: An off-track loop along the Capertee cliffline: a boot-shaped rock high above the valley, an old Aboriginal route through the cliffs, and a hidden sandstone tunnel.
hero_alt: A bushwalker standing on top of Mercurys Boot, a boot-shaped sandstone rock on the Capertee cliffline

intro: High above the Capertee Valley, a great sandstone block leans out over the drop. From the right angle it looks just like a boot. This loop takes you along the escarpment to Mercurys Boot, down through Baal Bone Gap and on to McLeans Pass, where a triangular tunnel cuts straight through the rock.

getting_there.intro: The aim is to park as close to Baal Bone Gap as you can. How close you get depends on your vehicle and how much risk you're happy to take on the fire trails.

options.heading: Moffitts Trail
options.text:
Head for Moffitts Trail (also signposted as Ben Bullen Trail). Conventional vehicles should stop wherever the track starts to look too rough for them.

Four-wheel drives can usually get to a sharp corner and steep descent about 1 km before the junction with the Bicentennial National Trail. Don't drive down unless you're confident you can drive back up.

options.heading: Unnamed junction
options.text: There's a good place to park at an unnamed junction a couple of kilometres south of Baal Bone Creek.

getting_there.note: Fire trail conditions change quickly after rain. Check the current NPWS alerts for Gardens of Stone National Park before you go.

walk_intro: The route has no formed track. Expect scrub, rock platforms and some route-finding, with the cliffline as your guide.

stops.heading: To the Capertee cliffline
stops.text: Leave Moffitts Trail and head cross-country to the Capertee cliffline. When you reach the cliff edge, follow it down towards the valley. The escarpment guides you most of the way, and the views open up over the Capertee Valley as you go.

stops.heading: Mercurys Boot
stops.text: Keep going along the cliffline until you reach Mercurys Boot. You'll know it when you see it: a big rock jutting out over the valley, shaped unmistakably like a boot. It's a great place for a break and photos.
stops.image_alt: A walker standing on top of Mercurys Boot against a clear blue sky
stops.caption: Standing on top of Mercurys Boot, high above the Capertee Valley

stops.heading: Baal Bone Gap
stops.text: Just below the Boot is Baal Bone Gap, a natural break in the cliffs and an easy way down into the valley. You may find water in one of the pipes at the Gap, but the tap may now be locked, so don't rely on it.

stops.heading: McLeans Pass
stops.text: From Baal Bone Gap, head east, roughly following the cliffline for a kilometre or so, until you reach McLeans Pass. There's a bit of a drop to get into the pass.

stops.heading: Stargate Tunnel
stops.text: Once you're at the bottom of the pass, head a little south to the Stargate Tunnel. This triangular sandstone tunnel is one of the highlights of the walk.
stops.image_alt: Looking through the triangular Stargate Tunnel towards ferns and forest beyond
stops.caption: Looking through the Stargate Tunnel

stops.heading: Back along the ridge
stops.text: From the Stargate Tunnel, climb back up to the ridgeline and follow it south until you reach the unnamed road. From there, the fire trails lead back to the Bicentennial National Trail and your car.

tips.heading: Off-track navigation
tips.text: This walk isn't signposted or marked. Carry a map and compass or GPS, and know how to use them.

tips.heading: Cliff edges
tips.text: The cliffs are high and sheer, and the edges can be undercut. Keep well back, especially with children or in wind.

tips.heading: Water
tips.text: Don't count on finding any. The tap at Baal Bone Gap may be locked, so carry all you'll need, particularly in summer.

tips.heading: Respect the country
tips.text: Baal Bone Gap has Aboriginal cultural sites, including hand stencils. Look, but don't touch. Leave no trace.

tips.heading: Tell someone
tips.text: Leave your plans with someone, and think about carrying a PLB. There's very little phone coverage out there.
